messages: Carla: CI is failing on docs/guides/setup.mdx — Docusaurus linkcheck flags a missing anchor and MDX parser errors. Snippet: Carla: ``` MDXParseError: Unexpected token at docs/guides/setup.mdx:42 linkcheck: ../ops/cache#warm-start -> anchor not found ``` Ben: Which exact lines? can you paste the tiny context? Carla: setup.mdx contains a fenced code example that includes a literal `:::note` (copied from a CONTRIBUTING example) which the MDX parser treats as an admonition start. The link points to `../ops/cache#warm-start` but the header on cache.mdx is `## Warm starting` so slug is `warm-starting`. Alice: Seen this before. Quick fixes: 1) escape or move the `:::` out of the fenced block; 2) add an explicit id on the target header e.g. `## Warm starting {#warm-start}`; 3) normalize the link to `#warm-starting`. Adding an HTML id is the least invasive for a backport. Greg: For fastest unblocking add `` under the heading. We'll tidy examples later. Ben: I'll take it. Plan: a) update the relative link to the correct slug b) move the admonition out of the fenced example (or escape it) c) run local linkcheck: `PYTHONPATH=. python -m scripts.linkcheck docs` before push. docs-ci: Note: CI previously failed because of cached build layers. If local linkcheck passes but CI errors, try clearing the cache or bumping the actions/cache key. Ben: Branch `docs/fix/admonition-anchor-1767` pushed. Cleared CI cache and retriggered build. CI passed after cache clear. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/4310 :white_check_mark: Carla: Thanks. Can you open a backport PR to `release/v1.x` using the HTML id shim only? Some customers still reference that branch. Ben: Yep, will open `backport/docs-1767` after merge. Alice: I'll add a tiny CONTRIBUTING note in a follow-up PR about not embedding raw admonition markers inside fenced code blocks and a short note on heading slug rules (e.g., "Warm starting" -> `warm-starting`). Saves future confusion. Carla: Perfect. Close after backport merges. :tada:
